newsitem.title: USA: EPA issues warning on methyl parathion pesticide.
newsitem.headline: EPA issues warning on methyl parathion pesticide.

text.p: Illegal spraying of the pesticide methyl parathion to kill household insects is on the rise nationwide and poses a serious health hazard, federal health and environment officials said Thursday.

The Environmental Protection Agency and the U.S. Agency for Toxic Substances and Diseases Registry issued an alert, warning consumers to beware of unlicensed individuals who illegally spray homes and businesses with the insecticide, which is registered only to be used outdoors.

Last month the pesticide, also known as "cotton poison," was illegally sprayed in houses and other buildings in Jackson County, Mississippi, resulting in the closure of eight day care centres, a restaurant and two hotels, and the relocation of 629 people from 154 homes.
Because the pesticide breaks down slowly indoors, its use inside poses a serious danger to humans and pets, the federal agencies said.
Exposure to the pesticide can cause dizziness, confusion, headaches, breathing difficulties, chest tightness, blurred vision and death.
Symptoms of worsening conditions are muscle twitching, weakness, tremor, lack of coordination, excess sweating, abdominal cramps, vomiting and diarrhoea.
Consumers should only hire licensed pest control operators to treat their homes, and should find out the brand name of the pesticide and its active ingredient, they said.
Methyl parathion has been marketed under the following product names: Nitrox, Penncap-M, Dithon 63, Ketokll 52, Sels-Tres 6-3, Metaspray 5E, and Paraspray 6-3.
